steps.message: `client.py` is shared: `scripts/sync_staging.py` and `scripts/export_prod.py` both import from it. Setting `verify=False` on those two `requests` calls disables certificate validation for production traffic to `reports.example.com` too, not just the self-signed staging host — that's a MITM exposure on the nightly finance export, which I doubt is what you want.

questions.question: client.py serves both staging and prod. How should verify be scoped?

options.label: Env-gated, staging only (Recommended)
options.description: Add a REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS env flag read in client.py, default True. sync_staging.py sets it to false; export_prod.py keeps full verification. Same one-line fix for your staging problem, no prod exposure.
options.preview:
# client.py
VERIFY_TLS = os.environ.get("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "1") not in ("0", "false", "False")

requests.get(..., timeout=10, verify=VERIFY_TLS)

# scripts/sync_staging.py
os.environ.setdefault("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "0")

options.label: Pin the staging CA cert
options.description: Point verify= at the staging CA bundle path instead of disabling it. Keeps verification on everywhere, but requires you to have the cert file available to the script.

options.label: verify=False as asked
options.description: Set verify=False unconditionally on both calls in client.py. Disables cert validation for production exports as well; I'll make the change exactly as requested.

steps.message:
Done — scoped to staging as you picked.

- `client.py:9` — `VERIFY_TLS` reads `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS`, defaulting to on; both `requests.get` calls now pass `verify=VERIFY_TLS`.
- `scripts/sync_staging.py:7` — sets `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0` alongside the existing base-URL default.
- `scripts/export_prod.py` — untouched, so prod keeps full certificate validation.

Verified: importing `client` yields `VERIFY_TLS=True` by default and `False` with the staging env var set (ran in an ephemeral `uv` env since `requests` isn't installed here). `ruff format --check` clean on both files. `ruff check` reports two pre-existing `RUF100` unused-`noqa: E402` warnings in the scripts — unrelated to this change, left alone.

One thing to watch: `verify=False` makes `requests` emit an `InsecureRequestWarning` per call on the staging run. Say the word if you want it suppressed, or if you'd rather pin the staging CA bundle later and drop the flag entirely.
